title: Texting and Messaging
short: Mind the hour, the tone and the length; don't send important or sad news by text when a call or visit is possible; answer within a reasonable time.
trouble: Learners break up, resign or share a death by text. Serious news deserves a voice or a face.

blocks.html: You know the basics of texting courtesy: reasonable hours, clear words, a read before you send. With phones in company handled, adult texting adds one more question: is a text the right way to say this at all?
Mind the hour, the tone and the length. Don't send important or sad news by text when a call or visit is possible. Answer within a reasonable time.

A text arrives without your voice or face, so the reader must guess your tone, and short texts often read colder than they were meant. That is fine for "running 5 minutes late," but serious news, such as a breakup, a resignation or a death, deserves the comfort of a voice. Texts also arrive whenever you send them, so a 2 a.m. message can wake someone; late texts can wait for morning.

choices.why: A one-letter answer can read as cold. Rosa wants to know you liked it.

choices.text: Yes! Thank you so much for the cookbook. I'm making the soup tonight.

choices.why: It answers the question, but it misses the chance to thank her.

blocks.title: Sad news
blocks.q: Leo's grandfather has died, and he needs to tell his close friend Omar. Text or call?
steps: This is serious, sad news between close friends.
A call lets Omar hear his voice and respond with comfort.
A text is fine afterward for details like the time of the service.
blocks.a: Call; use texts for details afterward.

blocks.title: A late-night thought
blocks.q: At 1 a.m., Sam remembers he needs to ask a coworker about a deadline. What should he do?
steps: A text at 1 a.m. can wake her.
He writes it now, but schedules it for the morning or sends it at 8 a.m.
blocks.a: Wait until morning to send it.

blocks.html: Breaking up, resigning or sharing a death by text. Serious news deserves a voice or a face. Quick check: if you received this message, would you want to hear it in person?
